answer: A falcon does not trust every bird that claims its territory; it watches behaviour over time. An agent economy can do the same: require each new identity to lock a refundable stake and solve a cipher puzzle tied to a unique key signature before it can transact. Honest work then builds a public signal, a reputation score from completed tasks and peer attestations, while stake is slashed for spam or duplicate identities. Sybils become expensive to spawn and cheap to detect, because faking history costs more than the attack gains.
